  3. reserved — otherwise, at least one hold on the tool is waiting.
  4. available — otherwise.

A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account. Because the test reads current facts, the order events arrive in doesn't matter. For example, a lapsed set-aside whose tool has already gone out to someone else is checked-out, even before its Hold Expired lands.

To match later events to a tool, the view also keeps, for each tool, the loan ID of the current loan and the hold ID and holder of each live hold. These are bookkeeping, not part of the row, and are never returned.

Queries

  • List the catalog. Takes nothing; it is the same for every neighbor (INV-TCAT-5). Returns every listed tool, each with toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt, status, dueDate, holdsWaiting, canCheckOut and canPlaceHold. There is no paging: the query always returns every listed tool, ordered by name, then by addedAt (INV-TCAT-13).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-TCAT-1: Every added tool appears in the catalog exactly once, available to borrow.
    • One entry per Tool Added. Nothing else creates an entry.
    • Each entry shows the tool's name, its description if it has one, and its default checkout period. Tools may share a name; each is its own entry.
    • A tool can be borrowed as soon as it is added.
  • INV-TCAT-2: A checked-out tool shows as checked out, with its due date, until it is returned.
    • When the loan is extended, the catalog shows the new due date.
    • The due date is cleared when the tool comes back.
  • INV-TCAT-3: A tool that is back in the shed with holds waiting, but not yet set aside, shows as reserved, never as available.
    • This covers the moment after a return before Hold Fulfilled lands, and the moment after a set-aside ends before the next hold is fulfilled.
    • The catalog doesn't show who it is reserved for. Only the holder whose turn it is can check it out; Check Out Tool enforces that (INV-CHK-3a).
  • INV-TCAT-4: A tool set aside for a holder shows as set aside until that holder checks it out or the set-aside ends.
    • A set-aside runs through the end of its collect-by date, the set-aside date plus 3 days, and lapses at the start of the next day, shed local time. It also ends early if the holder cancels the hold or closes their account.
    • The catalog shows the set-aside until Hold Expired is recorded. The holder's claim ends at the cut-off even if that is a little earlier; Check Out Tool enforces it (INV-CHK-3b).
    • However it ends, other than by the holder's checkout, the tool's status follows the status rules: checked-out if someone else already has it out, else reserved if another hold is waiting, else available.
  • INV-TCAT-5: The catalog is the same for every neighbor.
    • It never shows a neighbor that a tool is set aside for them; they see their own set-aside on My Holds.
    • It never shows who a tool is checked out to, who holds it, or who it is reserved or set aside for. Only the shed manager sees borrowers, on the Tool Inventory.
  • INV-TCAT-6: Each tool shows how many holds are waiting on it.
    • A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends.
  • INV-TCAT-7: The catalog offers Place Hold on any tool that isn't available: checked out, reserved, or set aside.
    • A neighbor who wants an available tool checks it out instead.
    • The action is offered by the tool's state alone. A neighbor who can't place the hold (they already hold the tool, have it on loan, or are suspended) still sees it, and Place Hold refuses them with the reason.
  • INV-TCAT-8: A retired tool drops off the catalog at once, including one retired while on loan.
    • Retiring a tool also ends its holds.
    • This differs from the Tool Inventory, which keeps a tool retired while on loan until it comes back or is recorded lost (INV-TINV-2). Neighbors can do nothing with a retired tool; the shed manager may still need to record it lost.
  • INV-TCAT-9: Only Tool Added, Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Hold Placed, Hold Cancelled, Tool Returned, Hold Fulfilled, Hold Expired, Tool Retired, Tool Lost and Neighbor Account Closed change the catalog.
    • Overdue notices, pickup emails and email changes are shown elsewhere, not here.
  • INV-TCAT-10: A tool recorded lost drops off the catalog.
    • Recording a tool lost ends its loan, retires it and ends its holds, all at once.
  • INV-TCAT-11: The catalog offers Check Out on an available, reserved or set-aside tool. It doesn't offer Check Out on a tool that is checked out.
    • The action is offered by the tool's state alone, the same to every neighbor. On a reserved or set-aside tool, only the holder whose turn it is can check it out; Check Out Tool refuses anyone else with the reason.
  • INV-TCAT-13: Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added.
    • The same order as every list in the shed.
  • INV-TCAT-12: Applying the same event twice leaves the catalog as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-TCAT-14: Any signed-in neighbor can read the Tool Catalog; a caller with no sign-in can't.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool added (INV-TCAT-1, INV-TCAT-11)
    • Given: the catalog lists no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a cordless drill, described as "18V, two batteries", with a 7-day default checkout period
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill, its description and its 7-day period, as available, with no holds waiting, Check Out offered and Place Hold not offered.
  • Two identical tools (INV-TCAT-1)
    • Given: the catalog lists one tool named "Cordless drill"
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a second tool named "Cordless drill", with its own tool ID
    • Then: the catalog lists both drills as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-TCAT-12)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill once, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: the same Tool Added, and the same Hold Placed, for the drill are applied again
    • Then: the catalog still lists the drill once, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Tool checked out (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-7, INV-TCAT-11)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill as available
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill, due 12 October
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October, with Place Hold offered and Check Out not offered. It doesn't show who borrowed it.
  • Loan extended (INV-TCAT-2)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for the drill's loan, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 19 October.
  • Hold placed (INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with no holds waiting
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for the drill
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Hold cancelled while the tool is out (INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for one of those holds
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Tool returned, no holds waiting (INV-TCAT-2)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 19 October, with no holds waiting
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available, with no due date.
  • Tool returned, holds waiting (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-7, INV-TCAT-11)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with no due date and 2 holds waiting, and offers both Check Out and Place Hold on it.
  • Only waiting hold cancelled while reserved (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for that hold
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available, with no holds waiting.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-TCAT-4, INV-TCAT-5, INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for the drill's front hold
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting, and offers Check Out and Place Hold on it. Every neighbor sees the same entry, including the holder it is set aside for.
  • Holder collects the set-aside tool (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill by the holder, due 24 October
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 24 October, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill by the holder at the front of the queue, due 24 October
    • Then: that holder's hold ends. The catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 24 October, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Set-aside expires, another hold waiting (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for the set-aside hold
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 1 hold waiting. Once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for that hold, it shows the drill as set aside, with no holds waiting.
  • Lapsed set-aside taken by someone else before the expiry lands (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, with Cara's hold waiting. Ben's collect-by date has passed, but Hold Expired has not been recorded.
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill by Cara, due 25 October, and then Hold Expired is recorded for Ben's hold
    • Then: after the checkout, the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 25 October, with no holds waiting. After the expiry, it still shows the drill as checked out, due 25 October. It never shows the drill as available or reserved.
  • Set-aside expires, no hold waiting (INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with no holds waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for the set-aside hold
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available.
  • Set-aside hold cancelled, another hold waiting (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for the set-aside hold
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Set-aside holder closes their account, no hold waiting (INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside for Cara, with no holds waiting
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Cara
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available.
  • Waiting holder closes their account (INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 2 holds waiting, one of them Cara's, and the hedge trimmer as checked out with 1 hold waiting, Cara's
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Cara
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill with 1 hold waiting and the hedge trimmer with none. Both are still checked out.
  • Tool retired in the shed (INV-TCAT-8)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill as available, and the ladder as available
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill
    • Then: the drill drops off the catalog. The ladder is unchanged.
  • Tool retired while on loan (INV-TCAT-8)
    • Given: the catalog shows the hedge trimmer as checked out, due 20 October, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the hedge trimmer
    • Then: the hedge trimmer drops off the catalog at once, though its loan carries on.
  • Retired tool's later events change nothing (INV-TCAT-8)
    • Given: the hedge trimmer was retired while on loan and has dropped off the catalog
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for its loan
    • Then: the hedge trimmer does not come back into the catalog.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-TCAT-10)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the drill drops off the catalog. Other tools are unchanged.
  • Events the catalog doesn't hear (INV-TCAT-9)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the drill's entry is unchanged.
  • Listing order (INV-TCAT-13)
    • Given: the catalog lists a ladder, then a cordless drill added on 1 October, then a second cordless drill added on 3 October
    • When: a neighbor lists the catalog
    • Then: the tools come back as: the cordless drill added 1 October, the cordless drill added 3 October, then the ladder.
  • Listing the catalog (INV-TCAT-5)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill (checked out, due 12 October, 1 hold waiting) and the ladder (available)
    • When: Ana lists the catalog, and then Ben does
    • Then: both get the same two tools with the same fields, with no paging, and nothing about who has borrowed or holds either tool.
  • No sign-in (INV-TCAT-14)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the catalog
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-TCAT-12). An event applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for a tool that is no longer listed: once a tool has been retired or recorded lost, its later events (a Tool Returned for a loan that carried on after retirement, or a replay) change nothing.
  • Hold events for a tool that is no longer listed: a hold can't be placed on a retired tool, and retirement ends its holds, so a hold event for an unlisted tool can only be a replay. It changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, Check Out on a tool someone else has just borrowed). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Tool Catalog is the neighbors' screen, for any signed-in neighbor; sign-in is handled outside the shed's events. It shows only tool details and state, the same to everyone.
  • PII & compliance: none. The catalog shows no neighbor's name, email or identity. The holders and borrowers it keeps for matching events are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Tool Added and the loan events' keys match slices/add-tool.md and slices/tool-inventory.md. The hold events and Neighbor Account Closed are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Check Out Tool and Place Hold.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":10,"name":"Return Tool","x0":1810.76,"x1":1954.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Return Tool

Intent

Let a borrower bring a tool back and end their loan themselves, from My Loans. The tool is then back in the shed, for the next holder or for anyone to borrow. The return records whether it was late, which is what counts toward a neighbor being flagged.

Trigger & Actor

The borrower, from their own My Loans screen, for one of their own loans. My Loans offers Return on every loan it lists (INV-MYL-12), including overdue loans, loans whose tool was retired while out, and loans of a suspended neighbor. The shed manager does not record returns; a tool that never comes back is recorded lost instead (Record Tool Lost).

Command / Input

Command: Return Tool

A NeighborId or LoanId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor returning, who must be the one making the request and the loan's borrower (INV-RET-1).
loanId LoanId yes The loan to end. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-RET-11), and still out (INV-RET-2).

There is no field for the tool's condition: nothing about it is recorded on return. A damaged tool is the shed manager's to retire.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Loans @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Returned → context Loans Read by: My Loans (the loan drops off), Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the tool is back in the shed), Holds To Fulfill (a returned tool with holds waiting), Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices (the loan has ended), and Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors (whether the return was late, and the late return behind a flag).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
toolId ToolId yes The loan's tool, from its Tool Checked Out. Carried so views about tools and holds match on the tool directly.
toolName Text yes Set by the system: the tool's name on the loan's Tool Checked Out.
neighborId NeighborId yes Set by the system: the borrower on the loan's Tool Checked Out (the same as the command's, by INV-RET-1). Carried so readers about neighbors match on the borrower directly.
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (Tool Checked Out.dueDate, moved by any Loan Extended), the date late was judged against.
returnedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.
returnedOn Date yes Set by the system: the calendar date of returnedAt in the shed's local time zone.
late Bool yes Set by the system: yes when returnedOn is after the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (INV-RET-4).

The event never changes. returnedOn and late are worked out once, by the command's handler, so every view reads the same answer.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Returned ends the loan in My Loans, Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices; puts the tool back in the shed on Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (or drops a tool retired while out); adds a tool with holds waiting to Holds To Fulfill; and gives Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors a late or on-time return. Each is specified in its own doc, and all are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Once a loan is returned, no overdue notice goes out for it (INV-OLN-4, Overdue Loans To Notify). A returned tool with no holds waiting is available to borrow straight away; one with holds waiting is reserved, and until Hold Fulfilled is recorded only the neighbor at the front of the queue may check it out (INV-CHK-3a, Check Out Tool). Late returns count toward a neighbor being flagged, 3 within 90 days (Neighbors To Flag). Those rules are owned by those slices.

  • INV-RET-1: The borrower returns their own loan themselves, from My Loans.
    • The request must come from the neighbor it names, and the loan must be theirs. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch. The shed manager does not record returns.
  • INV-RET-2: Only a loan that is still out can be returned, and only once.
    • A loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost can't be returned.
    • A closed account never has a loan out, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
  • INV-RET-3: Returning a tool records only Tool Returned.
    • Setting the tool aside for the first waiting hold is a separate system reaction to the return, recorded as Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold).
  • INV-RET-4: A return is late when it happens after the loan's due date: from the start of the day after the due date, in the shed's local time.
    • A return on the due date itself is on time. The due date is the one in force at the moment of return: the latest Loan Extended's dueDate, or Tool Checked Out's if never extended.
    • Tool Returned records the answer as late, with the date of return as returnedOn.
  • INV-RET-5: An overdue loan can be returned.
  • INV-RET-7: A suspended neighbor can return a tool.
  • INV-RET-9: A tool retired while on loan can still be returned.
    • The return ends the loan as usual. The tool stays retired: it doesn't come back into the Tool Catalog or Tool Inventory, and no hold is waiting on it, because retiring it ended its holds.
  • INV-RET-10: Returning a loan that this borrower has already returned succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second return.
  • INV-RET-11: The loan must have been checked out.
  • INV-RET-12: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: on-time return, no holds (INV-RET-1, INV-RET-3, INV-RET-4)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has the cordless drill (T1) on loan L1, due 12 October, and no holds are waiting on it
    • When: at 15:00 on 11 October, shed time, Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1, with toolId T1, the time it was recorded, returnedOn 11 October, and late no. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Return on the due date (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 12 October, late no.
  • Late return (INV-RET-4, INV-RET-5)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 00:05 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 13 October, late yes.
  • Return after an extension (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Loan Extended moved its due date to 19 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 on 15 October
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with late no, judged against 19 October.
  • Return with a hold waiting (INV-RET-3)
    • Given: Ana has L1, and Ben's hold on T1 is at the front of the queue
    • When: Ana returns L1
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded. No Hold Fulfilled is recorded by this command; setting T1 aside for Ben is Fulfill Hold's.
  • Suspended neighbor returns a tool (INV-RET-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended and has L1 out
    • When: Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1.
  • Returning a tool that was retired while on loan (INV-RET-9)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder (T2) on loan L2, and Tool Retired was recorded for T2 while it was out
    • When: Ana returns L2 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L2, with toolId T2. T2 stays retired.
  • The same return twice (INV-RET-10)
    • Given: Tool Returned was recorded for L1
    • When: Ana's same Return Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Loan already recorded lost (INV-RET-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for Ana's loan L3
    • When: Ana asks to return L3
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's loan (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: Ben asks, for himself, to return L1
    • Then: refused with not-your-loan: "You can only return your own loans." No event is recorded.
  • A request in someone else's name (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: a request from Ben asks to return L1 for Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only return loans for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown loan (INV-RET-11)
    • Given: no loan has ID L9
    • When: Ana asks to return L9
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-RET-12)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for returning a tool arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the borrower on the My Loans screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-RET-12): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-RET-1).
  3. loan-not-found (INV-RET-11).
  4. not-your-loan (INV-RET-1).
  5. If Tool Returned is already recorded for the loan, the request is a repeat: it succeeds and records nothing (INV-RET-10).
  6. loan-ended, if Tool Lost is recorded for the loan (INV-RET-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-RET-12
requester-mismatch You can only return loans for yourself. INV-RET-1
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-RET-11
not-your-loan You can only return your own loans. INV-RET-1
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-RET-2

requester-mismatch and loan-not-found can only come from a faulty or impersonating caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. The names mean the same conditions as in Extend Loan, and loan-ended uses the same sentence.

Suspension, an overdue loan and a retired tool never stop a return; there is no refusal for them.

Idempotency: a return is identified by its loan. A repeat after the loan was returned succeeds and records nothing. A loan ended by Tool Lost is refused, because returning it would be a different outcome from the one recorded.

Requests at the same moment: each Return Tool is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time per loan. Of a return and a Record Tool Lost for the same loan at once, whichever is decided first is recorded; the other finds the loan ended (a return then gets loan-ended, or succeeds as a repeat if the first was itself a return).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a borrower may return only their own loans (INV-RET-1); the shed manager doesn't record returns. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Returned holds no name or email; it records which loan ended, when, and whether it was late.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (this slice): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/extend-loan.md. Record Tool Lost is specified in a slice not yet written in depth; it is checked against this key when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans, Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, Holds To Fulfill, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors. Fulfill Hold reacts to a returned tool with holds waiting.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded; Check Out Tool no longer feeds the merged Neighbors view, Return Tool does (2026-11-01)
"},{"index":11,"name":"Tool Inventory — tool returned","x0":1979.76,"x1":2123.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Tool Inventory

Intent

Shows the shed manager every tool in the shed on the Tool Inventory screen, and which of them are out on loan, to whom, and until when. It is the shed manager's working screen for tools: they add and retire tools from it, and record a tool lost when it is out and never coming back.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Tool Inventory screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per tool currently in the shed or out on loan, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Add Tool (Add Tool slice) — always offered.
    • Retire (Retire Tool slice) — offered on every listed tool that is not already retired (INV-TINV-7).
    • Mark lost (Record Tool Lost slice) — offered only on a tool that is out on loan (INV-TINV-6).

Read Model / View

  • View: Tool Inventory built from events: "Tool Added", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Tool Inventory screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual — an entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because each command checks its own rules when it runs.

One row per listed tool. ToolId, NeighborId and LoanId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

Field Type Source / Notes
toolId ToolId Tool Added.toolId.
name Text Tool Added.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
description Text Optional: absent when the tool was added without one. Tool Added.description.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int Tool Added.defaultCheckoutPeriodDays (1–30).
addedAt Instant Tool Added.addedAt.
onLoan Bool Derived: yes from Tool Checked Out for this tool until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan; no otherwise.
loanId LoanId Derived: Tool Checked Out.loanId while the tool is on loan; none once Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan lands. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerId NeighborId Derived: Tool Checked Out.neighborId while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerName Text Tool Checked Out.neighborName while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
dueDate Date Derived: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for that loan, while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
retired Bool Derived: yes once Tool Retired is recorded for this tool. A retired row exists only while the tool is still out on loan.
canRetire Bool Derived: yes while retired is no. Returned so the screen can offer Retire (INV-TINV-7).
overdue Bool Derived: yes while the tool is on loan and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate; no otherwise (INV-TINV-9). Worked out when the inventory is read.
canMarkLost Bool Derived: same as onLoan. Returned so the screen can offer Mark lost (INV-TINV-6).

Queries

  • List the tool inventory. Takes nothing. Returns every listed tool, each with all the fields above. There is no paging: the query always returns every listed tool. Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added (addedAt); tools added at the same instant keep the order their Tool Added was recorded (INV-TINV-10).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-TINV-1: Every added tool appears in the inventory exactly once.
    • One entry per Tool Added; nothing else creates an entry.
    • Each physical item is its own tool, so two identical drills are two entries.
  • INV-TINV-2: A retired tool drops off the inventory once it is back in the shed or recorded lost.
    • A tool retired while it is in the shed drops off at once.
    • A tool retired while it is out on loan stays listed, marked retired and out, until it is returned or recorded lost. Then it drops off. This lets the shed manager record it lost if it never comes back.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that, so it drops off too.
    • This differs from the Tool Catalog, where a tool retired while on loan drops off at once: neighbors can do nothing with it, while the shed manager may still need to record it lost.
  • INV-TINV-3: The inventory changes only when a tool is added, checked out, extended, returned, retired or recorded lost.
    • The borrower's name shown on a tool that is out comes with Tool Checked Out.
    • Holds and overdue notices leave it unchanged. Hold state is shown to neighbors on the Tool Catalog, not here.
    • A tool's details never change after it is added (see the note under Add Tool's event table). A mistake is corrected by retiring the tool and adding it again.
  • INV-TINV-4: Each entry shows the tool's name, its description when it has one, and its default checkout period.
  • INV-TINV-5: Each entry shows whether the tool is out on loan. A tool that is out also shows the borrower's name and the due date.
    • A tool is out from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost.
    • The due date moves with each extension.
    • When the tool comes back or is recorded lost, the borrower's name and due date are no longer shown on it.
  • INV-TINV-6: The inventory offers "mark lost" only on a tool that is out on loan.
    • Recording a tool lost ends its loan, retires the tool and ends its holds. It never counts as a late return for the borrower (Record Tool Lost).
  • INV-TINV-7: The inventory offers "retire" on every listed tool that is not already retired.
    • A tool retired while out on loan stays listed but is not offered "retire" again.
  • INV-TINV-8: Applying the same event twice leaves the inventory as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-TINV-9: A tool that is out shows whether its loan is overdue.
    • Overdue means today's date in the shed's local time zone is after the due date in force. It is worked out when the inventory is read; no event marks a loan overdue.
  • INV-TINV-10: Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added.
    • Tools with the same name are in the order they were added; tools added at the same instant keep the order their Tool Added was recorded.
  • INV-TINV-11: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-TINV-12: Only the shed manager can read the Tool Inventory: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool added (INV-TINV-1, INV-TINV-4, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a cordless drill, described as "18V, two batteries", with a default checkout period of 7 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill with its description and its 7-day default checkout period, in the shed, with "retire" offered and no "mark lost".
  • Tool added without a description (INV-TINV-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a ladder with no description and a default checkout period of 3 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the ladder with its 3-day default checkout period and no description.
  • Two of the same tool (INV-TINV-1)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists one cordless drill
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a second cordless drill, with its own tool ID
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists both drills as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-TINV-8)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill once
    • When: the same Tool Added for that drill is applied again
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the drill once.
  • Tool checked out (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill, in the shed
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for Ana Ruiz borrowing the drill, due 12 October, carrying her name
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as out on loan to Ana Ruiz, due 12 October, and offers "mark lost" on it.
  • Loan extended (INV-TINV-5)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for Ana's drill loan, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October.
  • Tool returned (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as in the shed, with no borrower, due date or "mark lost".
  • Tool retired (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists a cordless drill and a ladder, both in the shed
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the cordless drill
    • Then: the cordless drill drops off the Tool Inventory, and the ladder is still listed.
  • Tool retired while out on loan (INV-TINV-2, INV-TINV-6, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder out on loan to Ben, due 20 October
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the ladder
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the ladder, marked retired and out on loan to Ben, due 20 October, with "mark lost" still offered and "retire" no longer offered.
  • Retired tool comes back (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Retired tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the hedge trimmer out on loan to Ana
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ana's hedge trimmer loan
    • Then: the hedge trimmer drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Out tool becomes overdue (INV-TINV-9)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: the inventory is read at 23:59 on 12 October, and again at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: the drill shows not overdue on the first read and overdue on the second. Nothing is recorded.
  • List order (INV-TINV-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for "Ladder", then "Cordless drill", then a second "Cordless drill"
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the tool inventory
    • Then: the order is the first "Cordless drill", the second "Cordless drill", then "Ladder".
  • Holds and notices don't change it (INV-TINV-3)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben on the drill, and later Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the drill's entry is unchanged.
  • Listing the inventory
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill (in the shed) and the ladder (out on loan to Ben, due 20 October)
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the tool inventory
    • Then: both tools are returned with all their fields, with no paging.
  • Not signed in (INV-TINV-11)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: the tool inventory is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-TINV-12)
    • Given: a neighbor is signed in, without the shed-manager role
    • When: the tool inventory is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see the tool inventory." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-TINV-11).
  2. not-shed-manager (INV-TINV-12).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-TINV-11
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can see the tool inventory. INV-TINV-12
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-TINV-8). A Tool Added, Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Tool Returned, Tool Retired or Tool Lost applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for a tool that is no longer listed: under the rules above, a Loan Extended, Tool Returned or Tool Lost can reach this view for a tool that is no longer listed only as a replay of an event already applied. It changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, "mark lost" on a tool that has just been returned). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Tool Inventory is the shed manager's screen; neighbors see tools on the Tool Catalog instead. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager (INV-TINV-12), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-TINV-11).
  • PII & compliance: shows a borrower's name while they have a tool out. It never shows their email. The name stops being shown on that tool once the loan ends.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, neighborName, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, toolId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId.
    • All but Tool Added are specified in slices not yet written in depth. These names are this view's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Add Tool, Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":12,"name":"Tool Catalog — tool returned","x0":2148.76,"x1":2292.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Tool Catalog

Intent

Shows neighbors every tool they can borrow or hold, on the Tool Catalog screen, and what state each one is in: available, checked out (and until when), reserved for the hold queue, or set aside for a holder. It is the neighbors' working screen for tools: they check tools out and place holds from it.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening the Tool Catalog screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per tool that is in the shed or out on loan and not retired, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Every neighbor sees exactly the same catalog (INV-TCAT-5). Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Check Out (Check Out Tool slice) — offered by the tool's state alone (INV-TCAT-11).
    • Place Hold (Place Hold slice) — offered by the tool's state alone (INV-TCAT-7).

Read Model / View

  • View: Tool Catalog built from events: "Tool Added", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Hold Placed", "Hold Cancelled", "Tool Returned", "Hold Fulfilled", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Tool Catalog screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because Check Out Tool and Place Hold each check their own rules when they run.

One row per listed tool. ToolId, LoanId, HoldId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be empty.

Field Type Source / Notes
toolId ToolId Tool Added.toolId.
name Text Tool Added.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
description Text Optional. Tool Added.description.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int Tool Added.defaultCheckoutPeriodDays: whole days, 1–30.
addedAt Instant Tool Added.addedAt.
status Text One of available, checked-out, reserved, set-aside. Derived: see the status rules below.
dueDate Date Optional. Derived: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for that loan, while status is checked out; none otherwise.
holdsWaiting Int Derived: the number of this tool's holds that have been placed and have neither been fulfilled nor ended.
canCheckOut Bool Derived: yes unless status is checked out (INV-TCAT-11).
canPlaceHold Bool Derived: yes unless status is available (INV-TCAT-7).

Status rules. A tool's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. checked-out — a loan of the tool is open: Tool Checked Out has been recorded, and neither Tool Returned nor Tool Lost for that loan.
  2. set-aside — otherwise, a hold on the tool has been fulfilled and has not yet ended.
  3. reserved — otherwise, at least one hold on the tool is waiting.
  4. available — otherwise.

A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account. Because the test reads current facts, the order events arrive in doesn't matter. For example, a lapsed set-aside whose tool has already gone out to someone else is checked-out, even before its Hold Expired lands.

To match later events to a tool, the view also keeps, for each tool, the loan ID of the current loan and the hold ID and holder of each live hold. These are bookkeeping, not part of the row, and are never returned.

Queries

  • List the catalog. Takes nothing; it is the same for every neighbor (INV-TCAT-5). Returns every listed tool, each with toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt, status, dueDate, holdsWaiting, canCheckOut and canPlaceHold. There is no paging: the query always returns every listed tool, ordered by name, then by addedAt (INV-TCAT-13).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-TCAT-1: Every added tool appears in the catalog exactly once, available to borrow.
    • One entry per Tool Added. Nothing else creates an entry.
    • Each entry shows the tool's name, its description if it has one, and its default checkout period. Tools may share a name; each is its own entry.
    • A tool can be borrowed as soon as it is added.
  • INV-TCAT-2: A checked-out tool shows as checked out, with its due date, until it is returned.
    • When the loan is extended, the catalog shows the new due date.
    • The due date is cleared when the tool comes back.
  • INV-TCAT-3: A tool that is back in the shed with holds waiting, but not yet set aside, shows as reserved, never as available.
    • This covers the moment after a return before Hold Fulfilled lands, and the moment after a set-aside ends before the next hold is fulfilled.
    • The catalog doesn't show who it is reserved for. Only the holder whose turn it is can check it out; Check Out Tool enforces that (INV-CHK-3a).
  • INV-TCAT-4: A tool set aside for a holder shows as set aside until that holder checks it out or the set-aside ends.
    • A set-aside runs through the end of its collect-by date, the set-aside date plus 3 days, and lapses at the start of the next day, shed local time. It also ends early if the holder cancels the hold or closes their account.
    • The catalog shows the set-aside until Hold Expired is recorded. The holder's claim ends at the cut-off even if that is a little earlier; Check Out Tool enforces it (INV-CHK-3b).
    • However it ends, other than by the holder's checkout, the tool's status follows the status rules: checked-out if someone else already has it out, else reserved if another hold is waiting, else available.
  • INV-TCAT-5: The catalog is the same for every neighbor.
    • It never shows a neighbor that a tool is set aside for them; they see their own set-aside on My Holds.
    • It never shows who a tool is checked out to, who holds it, or who it is reserved or set aside for. Only the shed manager sees borrowers, on the Tool Inventory.
  • INV-TCAT-6: Each tool shows how many holds are waiting on it.
    • A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends.
  • INV-TCAT-7: The catalog offers Place Hold on any tool that isn't available: checked out, reserved, or set aside.
    • A neighbor who wants an available tool checks it out instead.
    • The action is offered by the tool's state alone. A neighbor who can't place the hold (they already hold the tool, have it on loan, or are suspended) still sees it, and Place Hold refuses them with the reason.
  • INV-TCAT-8: A retired tool drops off the catalog at once, including one retired while on loan.
    • Retiring a tool also ends its holds.
    • This differs from the Tool Inventory, which keeps a tool retired while on loan until it comes back or is recorded lost (INV-TINV-2). Neighbors can do nothing with a retired tool; the shed manager may still need to record it lost.
  • INV-TCAT-9: Only Tool Added, Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Hold Placed, Hold Cancelled, Tool Returned, Hold Fulfilled, Hold Expired, Tool Retired, Tool Lost and Neighbor Account Closed change the catalog.
    • Overdue notices, pickup emails and email changes are shown elsewhere, not here.
  • INV-TCAT-10: A tool recorded lost drops off the catalog.
    • Recording a tool lost ends its loan, retires it and ends its holds, all at once.
  • INV-TCAT-11: The catalog offers Check Out on an available, reserved or set-aside tool. It doesn't offer Check Out on a tool that is checked out.
    • The action is offered by the tool's state alone, the same to every neighbor. On a reserved or set-aside tool, only the holder whose turn it is can check it out; Check Out Tool refuses anyone else with the reason.
  • INV-TCAT-13: Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added.
    • The same order as every list in the shed.
  • INV-TCAT-12: Applying the same event twice leaves the catalog as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-TCAT-14: Any signed-in neighbor can read the Tool Catalog; a caller with no sign-in can't.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool added (INV-TCAT-1, INV-TCAT-11)
    • Given: the catalog lists no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a cordless drill, described as "18V, two batteries", with a 7-day default checkout period
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill, its description and its 7-day period, as available, with no holds waiting, Check Out offered and Place Hold not offered.
  • Two identical tools (INV-TCAT-1)
    • Given: the catalog lists one tool named "Cordless drill"
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a second tool named "Cordless drill", with its own tool ID
    • Then: the catalog lists both drills as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-TCAT-12)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill once, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: the same Tool Added, and the same Hold Placed, for the drill are applied again
    • Then: the catalog still lists the drill once, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Tool checked out (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-7, INV-TCAT-11)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill as available
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill, due 12 October
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October, with Place Hold offered and Check Out not offered. It doesn't show who borrowed it.
  • Loan extended (INV-TCAT-2)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for the drill's loan, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 19 October.
  • Hold placed (INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with no holds waiting
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for the drill
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Hold cancelled while the tool is out (INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for one of those holds
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Tool returned, no holds waiting (INV-TCAT-2)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 19 October, with no holds waiting
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available, with no due date.
  • Tool returned, holds waiting (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-7, INV-TCAT-11)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with no due date and 2 holds waiting, and offers both Check Out and Place Hold on it.
  • Only waiting hold cancelled while reserved (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for that hold
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available, with no holds waiting.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-TCAT-4, INV-TCAT-5, INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for the drill's front hold
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting, and offers Check Out and Place Hold on it. Every neighbor sees the same entry, including the holder it is set aside for.
  • Holder collects the set-aside tool (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill by the holder, due 24 October
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 24 October, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill by the holder at the front of the queue, due 24 October
    • Then: that holder's hold ends. The catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 24 October, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Set-aside expires, another hold waiting (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for the set-aside hold
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 1 hold waiting. Once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for that hold, it shows the drill as set aside, with no holds waiting.
  • Lapsed set-aside taken by someone else before the expiry lands (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, with Cara's hold waiting. Ben's collect-by date has passed, but Hold Expired has not been recorded.
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill by Cara, due 25 October, and then Hold Expired is recorded for Ben's hold
    • Then: after the checkout, the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 25 October, with no holds waiting. After the expiry, it still shows the drill as checked out, due 25 October. It never shows the drill as available or reserved.
  • Set-aside expires, no hold waiting (INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with no holds waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for the set-aside hold
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available.
  • Set-aside hold cancelled, another hold waiting (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for the set-aside hold
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Set-aside holder closes their account, no hold waiting (INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside for Cara, with no holds waiting
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Cara
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available.
  • Waiting holder closes their account (INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 2 holds waiting, one of them Cara's, and the hedge trimmer as checked out with 1 hold waiting, Cara's
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Cara
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill with 1 hold waiting and the hedge trimmer with none. Both are still checked out.
  • Tool retired in the shed (INV-TCAT-8)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill as available, and the ladder as available
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill
    • Then: the drill drops off the catalog. The ladder is unchanged.
  • Tool retired while on loan (INV-TCAT-8)
    • Given: the catalog shows the hedge trimmer as checked out, due 20 October, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the hedge trimmer
    • Then: the hedge trimmer drops off the catalog at once, though its loan carries on.
  • Retired tool's later events change nothing (INV-TCAT-8)
    • Given: the hedge trimmer was retired while on loan and has dropped off the catalog
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for its loan
    • Then: the hedge trimmer does not come back into the catalog.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-TCAT-10)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the drill drops off the catalog. Other tools are unchanged.
  • Events the catalog doesn't hear (INV-TCAT-9)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the drill's entry is unchanged.
  • Listing order (INV-TCAT-13)
    • Given: the catalog lists a ladder, then a cordless drill added on 1 October, then a second cordless drill added on 3 October
    • When: a neighbor lists the catalog
    • Then: the tools come back as: the cordless drill added 1 October, the cordless drill added 3 October, then the ladder.
  • Listing the catalog (INV-TCAT-5)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill (checked out, due 12 October, 1 hold waiting) and the ladder (available)
    • When: Ana lists the catalog, and then Ben does
    • Then: both get the same two tools with the same fields, with no paging, and nothing about who has borrowed or holds either tool.
  • No sign-in (INV-TCAT-14)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the catalog
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-TCAT-12). An event applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for a tool that is no longer listed: once a tool has been retired or recorded lost, its later events (a Tool Returned for a loan that carried on after retirement, or a replay) change nothing.
  • Hold events for a tool that is no longer listed: a hold can't be placed on a retired tool, and retirement ends its holds, so a hold event for an unlisted tool can only be a replay. It changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, Check Out on a tool someone else has just borrowed). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Tool Catalog is the neighbors' screen, for any signed-in neighbor; sign-in is handled outside the shed's events. It shows only tool details and state, the same to everyone.
  • PII & compliance: none. The catalog shows no neighbor's name, email or identity. The holders and borrowers it keeps for matching events are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Tool Added and the loan events' keys match slices/add-tool.md and slices/tool-inventory.md. The hold events and Neighbor Account Closed are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Check Out Tool and Place Hold.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":13,"name":"My Loans — tool returned","x0":2317.76,"x1":2461.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: My Loans

Intent

Shows a neighbor the tools they have out right now, when each is due back, and anything that stands in the way of keeping a tool longer: the loan is overdue, someone else is waiting for the tool, or the tool has been retired. It also shows whether an overdue notice was sent or couldn't be delivered. It is the screen the neighbor extends and returns loans from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Loans screen.
  • Whose loans it shows: the loans of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Return (Return Tool slice) — offered on every listed loan (INV-MYL-12).
    • Extend (Extend Loan slice) — offered while canExtend is yes (INV-MYL-9, INV-MYL-10).

Read Model / View

  • View: My Loans built from events: "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Hold Placed", "Hold Cancelled", "Overdue Notice Sent", "Overdue Notice Failed", "Tool Returned", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the My Loans screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). overdue is worked out when the view is read, from dueDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Extend Loan and Return Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per open loan. ToolId, LoanId, HoldId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

Field Type Source / Notes
loanId LoanId Tool Checked Out.loanId.
neighborId NeighborId Tool Checked Out.neighborId: the borrower.
toolId ToolId Tool Checked Out.toolId.
toolName Text Tool Checked Out.toolName.
checkedOutAt Instant Tool Checked Out.checkedOutAt. Shown as the checkout date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.
dueDate Date Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for this loan.
overdue Bool Derived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate (INV-MYL-4). Worked out when the view is read.
overdueNotice Text One of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for this loan, undelivered once Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYL-5).
holdWaiting Bool Derived: yes while at least one hold on toolId is waiting (INV-MYL-9). See the hold rules below.
toolRetired Bool Derived: yes once Tool Retired is recorded for toolId (INV-MYL-10).
canExtend Bool Derived: yes unless overdue, holdWaiting or toolRetired is yes (INV-MYL-9, INV-MYL-10). Worked out when the view is read, because overdue is.

Hold rules. A hold on the loan's tool is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. This view doesn't hear Hold Fulfilled, and doesn't need to: a tool out on loan has no fulfilled hold, except in the brief gap described under Alternate & Error Flows. So here a hold counts as waiting from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when:

  • Hold Cancelled is recorded for it;
  • Hold Expired is recorded for it;
  • its holder checks the tool out (Tool Checked Out for this tool by the hold's neighbor);
  • Tool Retired or Tool Lost is recorded for the tool;
  • Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for the holder.

Holds placed before the loan began count the same as holds placed during it. To apply these rules, the view keeps, for each tool, the hold ID and holder of each hold that hasn't ended. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and is never returned.

Queries

  • List my loans. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every open loan whose borrower is that neighbor, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's loans (INV-MYL-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no open loans gets an empty list. Loans are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the loan was checked out (checkedOutAt); loans checked out at the same instant keep the order their Tool Checked Out was recorded (INV-MYL-13).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-MYL-1: A neighbor's My Loans shows only that neighbor's own loans.
    • The query returns only loans whose borrower is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else has a tool or who is waiting for one. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYL-2: Every checkout appears on the borrower's My Loans as one loan, with the tool and its due date.
    • The due date is the one Tool Checked Out carries. How it is set is Check Out Tool's rule.
    • A holder collecting a tool set aside for them is an ordinary checkout and appears the same way.
  • INV-MYL-3: When a loan is extended, its due date on My Loans becomes the extended due date.
    • The new due date is the one Loan Extended carries. How far an extension moves it is Extend Loan's rule (INV-EXT-3).
  • INV-MYL-4: A loan shows as overdue from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, and not before.
    • Overdue is worked out by comparing the due date with today. No event marks a loan overdue, so the screen shows it overdue on the day after the due date with nothing recorded.
    • An overdue loan can't be extended (INV-EXT-5, Extend Loan), so once a loan is overdue it stays overdue until it ends.
  • INV-MYL-5: Once an overdue notice is sent for a loan, My Loans shows that the borrower was notified.
    • If the notice later fails to deliver, My Loans shows instead that the overdue notice couldn't be delivered.
  • INV-MYL-6: A returned loan drops off My Loans, and so does a loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost.
    • My Loans shows only what the neighbor has out now. It keeps no borrowing history.
  • INV-MYL-7: Each loan shows the tool, the checkout date, the due date, whether it is overdue, and whether an overdue notice has been sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • There is no "due soon" state. Overdue is the only state a loan shows besides on loan.
  • INV-MYL-8: A loan's entry changes only through its own checkout, extension, overdue notice, return or loss, and through holds starting or ending on its tool.
    • That is: Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Overdue Notice Sent, Overdue Notice Failed, Tool Returned, Tool Lost, Hold Placed, Hold Cancelled, Hold Expired, Tool Retired, and Neighbor Account Closed of a holder.
    • The tool's name comes with Tool Checked Out.
  • INV-MYL-9: While any hold is waiting on a loan's tool, My Loans shows that the loan can't be extended because someone is waiting.
    • A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, when the holder checks the tool out, when the tool is retired or recorded lost, or when the holder closes their account. A tool on loan has no fulfilled hold, so for a loan's tool a hold waits until it ends.
    • This includes holds that were already waiting when the loan began. When no hold is waiting any more, the loan can be extended again.
  • INV-MYL-10: An overdue loan, and a loan whose tool has been retired, are marked as not extendable.
    • A tool can be retired while it is on loan. The loan stays on My Loans until it is returned or the tool is recorded lost, like any other loan.
    • Suspension is not shown on My Loans. A suspended neighbor sees it on My Account, and Extend Loan refuses an extension they try with its own reason (INV-EXT-7, Extend Loan).
  • INV-MYL-11: Applying the same event twice leaves My Loans as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYL-12: My Loans offers Return on every loan it lists, because Return Tool accepts a return for every open loan.
    • That includes overdue loans (INV-RET-5), loans of a suspended neighbor (INV-RET-7) and loans whose tool has been retired (INV-RET-9). The screen offers the action; nothing in this slice's view or query decides it, and Return Tool, not My Loans, is where a return is refused.
  • INV-MYL-13: Loans are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were checked out.
  • INV-MYL-14: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYL-15: My Loans is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool checked out (INV-MYL-2, INV-MYL-7, INV-MYL-12)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has no loans, and the cordless drill (T1) has no holds
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded at 10:00 on 5 October, shed time, for loan L1: Ana borrowing the drill, due 12 October
    • Then: Ana's My Loans lists L1: "Cordless drill", checked out 5 October, due 12 October, not overdue, overdue notice none, no hold waiting, extendable, with Return offered.
  • Loan extended (INV-MYL-3)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for L1, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: Ana's My Loans lists L1 due 19 October.
  • Not overdue on the due date (INV-MYL-4)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October
    • When: the list is read at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is not overdue, and is extendable.
  • Loan becomes overdue (INV-MYL-4, INV-MYL-10)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October, and the drill hasn't been returned
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 shows as overdue and not extendable. Nothing is recorded.
  • Overdue notice sent (INV-MYL-5)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans shows L1 as overdue, overdue notice none
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 shows overdue notice sent.
  • Overdue notice couldn't be delivered (INV-MYL-5)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans shows L1 with overdue notice sent
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 shows overdue notice undelivered.
  • Tool returned (INV-MYL-6)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1 (the drill) and L2 (a ladder)
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 drops off Ana's My Loans, and L2 is unchanged.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYL-6)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L2, overdue
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L2
    • Then: L2 drops off Ana's My Loans.
  • Someone places a hold on the borrowed tool (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October, with no hold waiting
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on the drill
    • Then: L1 shows a hold waiting and is not extendable. It doesn't say who is waiting.
  • One of two holds is cancelled (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from Ben's hold H1 and Cara's hold H2
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: L1 still shows a hold waiting, because H2 is.
  • The last waiting hold is cancelled (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from H2 only
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H2
    • Then: L1 shows no hold waiting and is extendable again.
  • The waiting holder closes their account (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from Ben's hold H1 only
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ben
    • Then: L1 shows no hold waiting.
  • Tool retired while on loan (INV-MYL-9, INV-MYL-10, INV-MYL-12)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from Ben's hold H1, due 12 October
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill
    • Then: L1 is still listed, due 12 October, with the tool retired, no hold waiting (retiring ended H1), not extendable, and Return still offered.
  • Loan starts with a hold already waiting (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: the drill was returned with Ben's hold H1 at position 1 and Cara's hold H2 at position 2, and it was set aside for Ben
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for loan L3: Ben collecting the drill
    • Then: H1 ends with Ben's checkout. Ben's My Loans lists L3 with a hold waiting, from H2, and not extendable.
  • Next loan after an expired hold (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: Ben's hold H1 on the drill was set aside for him and then Hold Expired was recorded for it. No other hold is waiting.
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for loan L4: Dan borrowing the drill
    • Then: Dan's My Loans lists L4 with no hold waiting, and extendable.
  • Other neighbors' loans (INV-MYL-1)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for loan L5: Ben borrowing a ladder
    • Then: Ben's My Loans lists L5, and Ana's My Loans is unchanged. Listing Ana's loans never returns L5.
  • Unrelated events don't change it (INV-MYL-8)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1 (the drill, T1), due 12 October, with no hold waiting
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana, and Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold on the ladder (T2)
    • Then: L1 is unchanged: still due 12 October, no hold waiting, extendable.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYL-11)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1 once
    • When: the same Tool Checked Out for L1 is applied again
    • Then: Ana's My Loans still lists L1 once, unchanged.
  • List order (INV-MYL-13)
    • Given: Ana checked out a ladder on 3 October, then a cordless drill on 5 October
    • When: her loans are listed
    • Then: the cordless drill comes first, then the ladder.
  • No loans (INV-MYL-1)
    • Given: Ana has no open loans
    • When: her loans are listed
    • Then: the list is empty.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYL-14)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Loans is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYL-15)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the loans of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own loans." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYL-14).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYL-15).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-MYL-14
requester-mismatch You can only see your own loans. INV-MYL-15
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYL-11). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a loan that has ended: once a loan is returned or its tool recorded lost, it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or an Overdue Notice Failed that arrives after the loan ended) changes nothing.
  • A lapsed set-aside that hasn't expired yet: after a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, someone else may check the tool out before Hold Expired is recorded for the lapsed hold. This view doesn't hear Hold Fulfilled, so until Hold Expired lands it counts that hold as waiting, and the new loan briefly shows a hold waiting. It clears when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, Extend just as a hold is placed, or Return just as the shed manager records the tool lost). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own loans (INV-MYL-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYL-15), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYL-14).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own loans only. It never shows who holds or is waiting for a tool. The holders it keeps for matching hold events are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, checkedOutAt.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Overdue Notice Failed (Record Overdue Notice Failure): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • The loan and hold events' keys match slices/tool-inventory.md and slices/tool-catalog.md. checkedOutAt matches Check Out Tool (slices/check-out-tool.md). The other events are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Extend Loan and Return Tool.

Open Questions

  • INV-MYL-12 (Return offered on every loan) has no enforcement site in this slice; rephrase it to cite Return Tool's INV-RET-5/7/9, which it relies on, or drop it (conformance 2026-11-01, uncertainty) — v2: kept and rephrased to cite INV-RET-5/7/9 and say the screen, not the view, offers it (2026-11-01)
"}],"rowLabels":{"x0":-14.240000000000002,"x1":113.75999999999999}}
